bib.title: Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024

read.skipped: References skimmed only; figure plots (Figs 2,4-7) are images, so only tables give numbers.

question: Can LMs reason better by writing code and, where the interpreter fails, simulating the output of non-executable lines with an LM, covering semantic as well as numeric reasoning?
hypothesis: LMs can leverage code-writing to improve Chain of Thought reasoning for semantic and mixed tasks, not just logic and arithmetic, if they selectively emulate the interpreter.
contributions: Chain of Code: LM writes code/pseudocode, an interpreter executes it line by line and an LM (LMulator) simulates lines that raise exceptions, sharing program state
84% on BBH with text-davinci-003 (+12 over CoT), above average human raters
Ablations showing both interpreter and LM simulation are needed
Applications to instruction-tuned chat models and robotics

method.summary: Few-shot prompting: the LM writes a program as reasoning steps; Python runs each line inside try/except, and on failure an LM is given question, prior lines and program-state history and generates the next state, which is written back to Python. Answer is the variable `answer`, or the LM's `A: answer` on irrecoverable error. No training.
method.task: multi-step reasoning (BIG-Bench Hard, GSM8K, robot manipulation)

datasets.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
datasets.split: per-task test questions with 3 few-shot examples; per-task question counts not stated
datasets.source: Suzgun et al. 2022 / Srivastava et al. 2022; human-rater baselines and CoT prompts provided by dataset

inference.prompting: Few-shot, 3 examples from the same task (single task) or 3 examples from different tasks (cross task); 1 example for robotics. Instruction-tuned: zero-shot system messages or a system message coercing completion-model behaviour plus 3 examples.

parameters.variants: Interweave (main), try Python except LM, try Python except LM state; ablations Python only, LM only, LM state
parameters.emulation: LMulator receives question, prior lines and state history and may use chain of thought
parameters.program_state_format: strings parsed into built-in Python types (dict, tuple)

other.decoding_settings_missing: temperature, sampling, max tokens, number of runs and seeds are not stated

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: percent of questions answered correctly, per task and averaged over the 23 BBH tasks

eval.protocol: Single run per setting as far as stated; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.

prompts.purpose: Zero-shot instruction-tuned: completion-model coercion system message
prompts.text: Pretend you are a completion model that is prompted with three examples. You should follow the pattern of these examples strictly. At the end of your reply, you should always output an answer

limits: Generate-then-execute with interweaving needs extra context length and computation time.
Code does not help on some semantic tasks, e.g. Ruin Names.
LM cannot modify custom Python objects while simulating; state is serialized as strings into built-in types.
Executes LLM-written code with Python as if benign; needs safeguards (impact statement).
Main model text-davinci-003 is a deprecated completion model; instruction-tuned results rely on coercion and the gap narrows with gpt-4.
Zero-shot comparison in Table A3 is unfair: CoC Interweave gets 3 examples, other columns none (authors concede).
Human raters had no code access; no seeds, sampling settings or CIs reported.
Cross-task on PaLM 2-S*: CoC no better than CoT (47 vs 47).
